newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher as soyoil surges.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher as soyoil surges.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher on Wednesday, boosted by short covering ahead of Thursday's U.S. Census and USDA export data and by gains in soyoil, traders said.

"Every Wednesday you're going to come in here and these export figures are going to make people nervous," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities in Iowa. "You cannot have anything above 200 (200,000 tonnes) on the beans. Anything over that is going to be bullish."
Analysts' estimates for Thursday's USDA exports ranged from 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.

Floor sources also pointed to ideas Thursday's U.S. Census oilmill data would show soybean crushings in March at 129.5 milion to 132 million bushels, compared with February's total of 125 million bushels.

A rally in soyoil also boosted soybeans. Floor sources cited fund buying in soyoil and rumors of export business in the works. They said crushing levels were expected to fall further in the coming weeks, diminishing stockpiles of soyoil.
CBOT soybeans closed 2-1/4 to one cent per bushel higher with May up two at $8.42-1/2 and new crop November up 1-1/2 at $6.96.

On the day, ADM bought three million bushels July, ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp bought one million May and ING bought one million July, pit sources said. Refco Inc sold one million November and bought one million July.
Rosenthal Collins spread five million bushels July/May at three cents, premium July, and Prudential Securities spread 2.5 million August/May at 14-1/2 cents, premium May, traders said.

In options trade, Prudential Securities bought 200 July $9.75 calls at six cents and sold 200 July $8.50 calls at 27-1/2 cents. Refco bought 200 July $8.00 puts at 13-1/4 and sold 200 July $7.75 puts at six cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 43,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 44,492.
